chunks: Ḥakam ibn Ḥukaym, the son of Khallād’s brother, asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and said:
I urinate and do not find water, and some urine gets on my hand. So I wipe it on the wall and on the dust. Then my hand sweats, and I touch my face, or some of my body, or it reaches my clothing.
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: dust or earth used here for wiping
key_terms.الْحَائِطِ: the wall used here for wiping
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it
key_terms.يَدِي: my hand, the part affected by impurity

ai.seo_question: If urine touches my hand and I cannot find water, is there any harm if I wipe it with dust and later touch my body or clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling concerning urine on the hand when water is unavailable and the person wipes it with a wall or dust. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm if the hand later sweats and touches the face, body, or clothing. The narration is relevant to rulings of najasah and ritual purity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.158 - Hakam ibn al-Hakim Akhi Khallad asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), saying to him: 'I urinate and do not find water, and some urine gets on my hand. I then wipe it on the wall or with dust. Later, my hand sweats, and I touch my face or some part of my body, or it touches my clothing.'
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'"
